findings.reason: an implementer following the contract with min 0.0 silently reintroduces a documented production hazard (producers ending on their first wake-up), and the done-when as written cannot catch it.
findings.text: The reader is specified as taking "the smallest accepted value", with "one below the minimum" giving the default (i.e. accept >= min), yet the same deliverable says "a lease takes a positive floor" while promising "no accepted value changes". `producer_lease_seconds` refuses zero today (`return value if value > 0 else PRODUCER_LEASE_SECONDS`, reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:683, and the same rule at reckon/crew/runs.py:1717), because that docstring records that "a lease of zero would end every producer on its first wake-up". With min=0.0 the lease begins accepting 0 — the exact value the code refuses — and any positive min other than an arbitrary epsilon changes other accepted values; either way the invariant the plan asserts is false for the lease site. The done-when only asserts that "a negative value gives that site's default", so it does not exercise the zero case and would pass while the hazard returned.

findings.reason: §12's own body names the wait a dispatcher needs, so the stale declaration misleads no node, but the document contradicts itself on a declaration a reader may trust.
findings.text: `plan-standalone` asserts the plan "waits on none", but §12 (docs/plans/the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches.html:254-258) declares that the critical-path coverage figure "belongs to work-scheduling-surface §3" and that "waiting costs a queue position", so the plan does wait on another plan's section.
